meta.triageRationale: One story in the daemon's workflow module. The pending list is one scan with a fixed set of kinds; BUILD joins it. The same story must make sure a BUILD record's document can be served to the review pane (the delivery snapshot marks a record 'review-view' only when its markdown carries the artifact marker, and build records are served read-only today) and that a decision on it goes through the existing approve path with its code-review rule. The plugin already knows the BUILD kind in its table. Seven BUILD records are pending in this repository now, so the list grows little. A few files in one module, one approach, few tasks.

summary.prose: A Story's build record now appears in the list of documents awaiting approval once the Story's code review has run. From then on it is in the review pane's table, opens there like any document (and by itself when a chat turn produces the code review), and can be approved or rejected from the pane; approving it completes the Story, under the same code-review rule as today. A build record rejected from the pane leaves the list for good: after the fixes the Story is completed by approving it in the chat, as today, since a later build run keeps the rejection on the record. A build record of a Story that is still being built, or whose code review has not run, is not listed. Acceptance: ac1, a build record that is neither approved nor rejected and whose Story has a code review record is in the pending list with kind BUILD, its work item id and the path of its BUILD.md; ac2, a build record without a code review record, and an approved or rejected one, is not listed, and EXTEND, STUB and AMD records stay out; ac3, the review pane opens and decides a build record through the existing calls, an approval the approve call withholds being relayed with its reason.

api.name: listPendingArtifacts

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: The repository whose .insrc/artifacts directory is scanned.

returns.meaning: As today, plus BUILD records. PENDING_KINDS becomes ['SPEC','DEF','HLD','LLD','PLAN','ISSUE','BUILD','CR'] and its comment says BUILD is listed once the Story's code review has run, with EXTEND, STUB and AMD still excluded. In the scan, a file BUILD-<x>.json passes the kind check and is then skipped unless the directory also holds CR-<x>.json (same suffix; the names come from the one readdirSync the scan already makes, held in a Set). The approved/rejected rule applies as to every kind. The descriptor is built by the existing toDescriptor: kind 'BUILD', title 'BUILD <work item id>' (a build record's body has no title), mdPath from deriveMdPath (which already resolves a BUILD record's BUILD.md), workItemId, openQuestionCount 0. One addition for a BUILD record only: its mdPath is the derived path only when that file exists AND its first 512 characters contain the marker '<!-- insrc:artifact <this record's artifact id> -->'; otherwise mdPath is ''. Two older shapes fail that test: a record without epicCreatedAt whose build began on a later day than its work item derives a folder that does not exist, and a BUILD.md written before the marker was introduced has none, so the content and decision calls could not resolve it. Such a record is listed by its id with no path, as a pathless record of any kind is today, and nothing is offered a path that cannot be opened or decided. This is one existsSync and one bounded read per listed BUILD record. The scan also sorts the directory's file names before walking them, so the list's order is the names' order on every platform (BUILD-<x> before CR-<x>).

errors.condition: An unreadable store directory throws (mapped to { error } by handleWorkflowPending); one malformed file is skipped and logged. The code review record is checked by name only, so a malformed CR file does not hide or fail the build record.

The JetBrains plugin also reads this list (DaemonGateway.pendingArtifacts) and approves through workflow.approve, which runs the same gate; it has no enumeration of pending kinds, so a BUILD row is carried by its kind text; this Story changes nothing there and its hand check does not cover it. alternativesConsidered.name: List a BUILD record once its Story has a code review record
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: BUILD joins the pending kinds, but a build record is listed only when the Story's code review has run
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add 'BUILD' to PENDING_KINDS. In listPendingArtifacts a BUILD-<x>.json that is neither approved nor rejected is listed only when CR-<x>.json exists in the same directory (whatever its verdict). The names of the directory's files are already read once per scan, so the check is a set lookup. Everything else (title, path, work item id) uses the existing descriptor code; the content and decision calls already serve a BUILD record.
pros: A build record appears when it is time to close the Story, which is when the user is asked to approve it
The review pane's auto-open then opens it at that moment, once, instead of at the Story's first task
A Story still being built adds nothing to the list
Filesystem only, one set lookup per BUILD record; no delivery graph is built
cons: A build record of a Story whose code review was never run is not listed (it cannot be closed under the code-review rule either, and is still on the delivery board)
The readiness rule is a second condition beside approved/rejected

alternativesConsidered.name: List every unapproved BUILD record
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: BUILD joins the pending kinds with no further condition
pros: Every open build is visible in the table
cons: A build record exists from the Story's first validated task, so the list shows records that cannot be approved yet
The auto-open would open the build record at the end of the turn that validated the first task, and never again when the Story is actually ready
Approving such a record from the pane is withheld or, with the code-review rule not enforced, closes a half-built Story
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Puts unfinished builds in a list of documents awaiting approval.

alternativesConsidered.name: List a BUILD record when every planned task has passed
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Readiness computed from the plan and the recorded task results
alternativesConsidered.approach: Build the Story's validation counts as the delivery read model does (plan tasks against recorded results) and list the BUILD record when none is failed or unrecorded.
pros: Readiness means exactly 'the build is done'
cons: The pending scan would read plans and results per build record or build the delivery graph, on a call the pane makes often
Two definitions of readiness to keep in step (the delivery model's and this one)
A done build without a code review still cannot be closed, so the user is offered an approval that is then withheld
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: More exact about 'built' but costlier and still offers an approval that is withheld.
